llm.domain: Mission reports, crew dossiers and incident reports published by the Meridian Deep Space Agency, a fictional deep-space exploration agency. Documents are written in a formal institutional register and consistently print an identifier in parentheses after the first mention of a person or vehicle.

Mission.description: A crewed mission flown by the agency, identified by its mission code.

instructions.document: This document IS a mission report. Extract the single mission that the report covers, which is the one named in the 'Mission code' header field.
instructions.chunk: Extract every mission explicitly named in this passage by its mission code, including missions only referred to in passing. Do not extract a mission that is merely alluded to without its code.

code.instructions: Uppercase letters, a hyphen, then the mission number, exactly as printed. Do not confuse it with an incident code (which starts with 'INC-') or a vehicle designation (which has exactly three letters).

designation.description: The descriptive name of the mission, as distinct from its code.
designation.instructions: Printed in the 'Designation' header field of a mission report.

status.description: The current status of the mission.
status.instructions: Printed in the 'Status' header field of a mission report. Use 'active' for a mission still under way.

summary.description: A concise summary of the mission's objective and outcome.
summary.instructions: Two or three sentences. Mention the objective, the vehicle flown and the outcome so far.

Astronaut.description: A member of the agency's flight crew, identified by their crew ID.

instructions.document: This document IS a crew dossier. Extract the single crew member that the dossier describes, named in the 'Name' and 'Crew ID' header fields.
instructions.chunk: Extract every crew member explicitly named in this passage together with their crew ID. If a passage refers to a person by surname alone, with no crew ID anywhere in the passage, do not extract them.

crew_id.description: The agency's unique crew identifier, printed in parentheses after a crew member's name.
crew_id.instructions: The literal 'MDSA-' prefix followed by four digits. Take it from the parenthesised identifier that follows the person's name, or from the 'Crew ID' header field of a dossier.

full_name.description: The crew member's full name, without rank or title.
full_name.instructions: Given name followed by surname. Strip ranks and titles such as 'Cmdr.', 'Lt.' or 'Dr.'.

specialty.instructions: Printed in the 'Specialty' header field of a dossier.

biography.description: A concise summary of the crew member's background and flight record.
biography.instructions: Two or three sentences. Mention when they joined the agency, their qualifications and the missions they have flown.

Spacecraft.description: A spaceflight vehicle operated by the agency, identified by its hull designation.
Spacecraft.instructions: Extract every vehicle explicitly named in this passage together with its hull designation. Vehicles are written as a name followed by the designation in parentheses, for example 'MDV Cassiopeia (VSP-03)'. Do not extract a vehicle class on its own, such as 'Vesper-class', as a vehicle.

designation.description: The vehicle's hull designation, printed in parentheses after its name.
designation.instructions: Exactly three uppercase letters, a hyphen, then two digits. Do not confuse it with a mission code (four or more letters) or a crew ID (which starts with 'MDSA-').

name.description: The vehicle's name, including the 'MDV' prefix.

vehicle_class.instructions: Usually stated next to the vehicle as '<Name>-class <kind>', for example 'Vesper-class crew transport'. Extract only the kind, not the class name.

Incident.description: A recorded in-flight anomaly, identified by its incident code.

instructions.document: This document IS an incident report. Extract the single incident that the report covers, named in the 'Incident code' header field.
instructions.chunk: Extract every incident explicitly named in this passage by its incident code. An anomaly described without an incident code is not an Incident.

code.instructions: The literal 'INC-' prefix followed by four digits.

title.description: The short title of the incident.
title.instructions: Printed in the 'Title' header field of an incident report.

severity.instructions: Printed in the 'Severity' header field of an incident report.

cause.description: A concise statement of what caused the incident.
cause.instructions: One or two sentences, drawn from the cause section of the report.

AssignedTo.description: A crew member serving on a mission.
AssignedTo.instructions: Only assert the assignment when the text says the person served on, flew, or commanded that mission. Do not infer it from the person merely being mentioned alongside the mission. A person may be assigned to more than one mission, in different roles.

role.description: The role the crew member served in on this mission.
role.instructions: Use the role stated for that specific mission. A person promoted between missions holds a different role on each.

notes.description: A short note on what the crew member did in this role.
notes.instructions: One sentence. Omit the field if the text says nothing beyond the role itself.
notes.examples: Flew all three relay node approaches manually after the automated approach system failed.

Operates.description: A mission flown using a particular spacecraft.
Operates.instructions: Only assert this when the text connects the vehicle to that specific mission. A vehicle mentioned for an unrelated reason, such as sharing a faulty component batch, is not operated by the mission under discussion.

note.description: A short note on how the vehicle was used on this mission.
note.instructions: One sentence. Omit the field if the text says nothing beyond the vehicle being flown.
note.examples: Certified for extended crewed operations beyond cislunar space on this flight.

OccurredDuring.description: An incident that took place in the course of a mission.
OccurredDuring.instructions: Only assert this when the text places the incident within that mission's flight. An incident mentioned in a mission report as background, without having occurred on that mission, does not qualify.

flight_day.description: The mission flight day on which the incident occurred.
flight_day.instructions: The number alone, without the words 'flight day'. Omit the field if the text does not state it.

impact.description: A short statement of how the incident affected the mission.
impact.examples: Deferred the release of relay Node C by six days.
